question: What is the most common cancer diagnosed among women in Nigeria?
explanation: Breast cancer has the highest incidence rates among women both locally in Nigeria and across global populations. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h1)

question: Why do many Nigerian women present with advanced stages of breast cancer at healthcare facilities?

options.A: Local hospitals completely lack any diagnostic tools
options.B: Financial constraints and cultural beliefs delaying care
options.C: The disease grows much faster in African populations
options.D: Early symptoms only appear during the terminal stage

explanation: Delays in seeking orthodox treatment are frequently linked to economic barriers, fear, and reliance on traditional remedies. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which anatomical structure provides main structural support and shape to the breast?
explanation: Cooper's suspensory ligaments connect the breast tissue to the dermis, providing structural support. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h2)

question: Where do the majority of breast malignancies typically originate?
explanation: Most breast cancers start in the epithelial cells lining the ducts and lobules of the glandular tissue. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which genetic mutations are strongly linked to an increased risk of hereditary breast cancer?
explanation: Inherited mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 tumor suppressor genes significantly elevate lifetime breast cancer risk. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h3)

question: Prolonged exposure to which hormone is a primary driver in many breast cancer cases?
explanation: Extended lifetime exposure to estrogen, from early periods or late menopause, stimulates cellular proliferation in breast tissue. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is the key difference between in situ and invasive breast cancer?

options.A: Invasive cancer only affects the skin of the nipple
options.B: In situ cancer immediately spreads to distant organs
options.C: In situ cells have not breached the basement membrane
options.D: Invasive cancer is entirely benign and non-cancerous

explanation: Carcinoma in situ is confined within the duct or lobule, whereas invasive carcinoma breaks through into surrounding tissue. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h4)

question: What does the letter 'N' stand for in the TNM cancer staging system?
explanation: In the TNM classification, N describes the extent of spread to regional lymph nodes. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h4)

question: Which physical characteristic describes a typical malignant breast lump found during palpation?

options.B: Hard, painless, and irregular in shape
options.C: Soft, mobile, and painful on touch

explanation: Malignant lumps are typically firm to hard, painless, fixed, and possess irregular borders. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h5)

question: What is the medical term for the dimpled, thickened skin appearance caused by lymphatic blockage in breast cancer?
explanation: Edema from blocked dermal lymphatics creates an orange-peel skin texture known as peau d'orange. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h5)

question: When is the best time for a menstruating woman to perform a breast self-examination?

options.A: On the first day of menstrual bleeding
options.B: Right before her menstrual bleeding starts
options.C: During the middle of her ovulation cycle
options.D: A few days after her monthly period ends

explanation: Hormonal swelling subsides after menstruation, making the breast tissue soft and easier to examine accurately. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h6)

question: Why is breast ultrasonography often preferred over mammography for younger women?

options.A: Mammography machines are completely unavailable in all health centers
options.B: Ultrasound can fully replace the need for tissue biopsies
options.C: Ultrasound uses high-dose radiation to kill cancer cells
options.D: Younger women have dense breast tissue that hides details on X-rays

explanation: Dense breast tissue limits mammogram sensitivity, making ultrasound an effective complementary imaging tool. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h6)

question: What is a key nursing intervention to prevent lymphedema after a left modified radical mastectomy?

options.A: Encourage heavy weightlifting exercises with the left arm
options.B: Elevate the left arm above the heart level all day
options.C: Apply tight elastic bandages continuously to the left hand
options.D: Avoid blood pressure measurements on the left arm

explanation: Avoiding trauma, venipuncture, and blood pressure measurements on the affected side prevents impaired lymphatic flow and lymphedema. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h7)

question: Which surgical procedure involves the removal of the entire breast tissue along with axillary lymph nodes?
explanation: A modified radical mastectomy removes the entire breast along with regional lymph nodes in the axilla. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of palliative care for a patient with terminal breast cancer?

options.A: Speeding up the natural terminal dying process
options.B: Curing the primary malignancy through aggressive chemotherapy
options.C: Improving quality of life and controlling distressing symptoms
options.D: Reversing distant organ metastasis in the liver and lungs

explanation: Palliative care focuses on relieving pain and suffering to ensure the best possible quality of life. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h8)

question: Which guideline framework is typically used to manage cancer pain effectively?
explanation: The World Health Organization analgesic ladder guides the stepwise administration of pain relief medications. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h8)

question: How do nurses contribute most effectively to secondary prevention of breast cancer in Nigeria?

options.A: Isolating diagnosed patients from their local communities
options.B: Performing complex surgical mastectomies in local health centers
options.C: Prescribing chemotherapy drugs during community outreaches
options.D: Conducting awareness campaigns and teaching early detection methods

explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early detection through community screening and education to catch disease early. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h9)

question: Which of the following is an example of a primary prevention strategy for breast cancer?

options.A: Encouraging regular physical exercise and healthy nutrition
options.B: Starting targeted hormonal therapy after surgery
options.D: Performing a monthly clinical breast examination

explanation: Primary prevention aims to prevent the disease from developing initially through lifestyle modifications. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h9)
